concept.title: Places
concept.shortdesc: How uFTi records a place, and how it helps you spell a place the same way each time.

conbody.p: In uFTi, a place is the words you type. There is no map, and no list of places to pick from. So type the place as your record gives it, such as a town or a parish.

section.title: Where you are asked for a place
section.p: You meet a place box in these forms:

ul.li: The place box in the details of an event.

section.p: They all work in the same way.

section.title: Typing a place
section.p: An empty box says . As you type, uFTi shows the places in this tree that match. It shows up to eight, underneath the box. Choose one to use it. Or keep typing a new place.

section.title: Spell it the same way each time
section.p: The places offered are the ones you have already typed in this tree. When you choose one, the place is spelled exactly as before. That keeps one place from turning into two.
When a record spells a place in a different way, type it as the record does. Then the tree shows what the record said.
